The speed of the progress in usability and features of FLOSS is quite surprising even for people like me that have been using it for over a decade. That's mostly due to at least two factors:

  • one is, obviously, that when you start from scratch, there' s a lot of room for improvement, and small things pile up very quickly to impressive changes;
  • the other is the positive feedback loop “better usability ⇒ more users ⇒ more developers ⇒ faster development ⇒ better usability”.

And of course as the user base expands hardware and software vendors are more pressed to look at the phenomenon as something bigger than just a hobbyist pastime, and their involvement does a lot, especially in terms of wider hardware support.
